about: Local state scenarios on a real filesystem (appendix A 48-50). Each scenario states the starting files, the action, and what must hold afterwards. Contexts are the query identity a file or handle is bound to.

collection.fact: --out writes NDJSON: a header line (query context, format version, started_at), then records, each page closed by a kind:page marker (cursor, ids, n, stop_reason, skipped, coverage). Only complete pages are trusted: on resume the tail after the last marker is dropped and re-read. A file for another query or an older format is refused before any byte changes. A marker whose ids or n disagree with the records above it is an integrity failure. The file is locked without waiting; writes are fsynced; --limit counts what is saved (parent comments for comments).

scenarios.name: new-file-gets-header
scenarios.after: first line is a header carrying context X and the current format; nothing else

scenarios.name: page-commit
scenarios.action: commit records [A, B] with cursor CUR1
scenarios.after: lines: header, A, B, page marker {ids:[A,B], n:2, cursor:CUR1}; the file is fsynced

scenarios.name: interrupted-tail-replayed
scenarios.start: header X, A, B, marker(A,B), C (no marker)
scenarios.after: C is dropped; resume continues from the marker's cursor; ids seen = {A, B}

scenarios.name: other-query-refused-byte-identical
scenarios.after: refused with an argument error naming another query; the file's bytes are unchanged

scenarios.name: older-format-refused-byte-identical
scenarios.start: header X with an older format, A, marker(A)
scenarios.after: refused as written by an earlier version; bytes unchanged

scenarios.name: previous-skill-file-refused
scenarios.start: a file written by the previous skill version (format 2 header)

scenarios.name: integrity-failure
scenarios.start: header X, A, B, marker {ids:[A], n:1}
scenarios.after: refused as an integrity failure; bytes unchanged

scenarios.name: complete-file
scenarios.start: header X, A, marker(A, stop_reason exhausted)

scenarios.name: dedupe-across-pages
scenarios.after: only B is written in the new page

scenarios.name: limit-counts-saved
scenarios.start: header X (comments), parent P1, reply R1, parent P2, marker
scenarios.after: two parents are already saved: nothing more is requested

handles.fact: A handle is a monotonically increasing number bound to its query context (command, target, order, filters, the Facebook account). The counter reservation is fsynced before the handle file is written, so a crash leaves a gap, never a reused number. Files are 0600 in a 0700 directory.

scenarios.name: counter-survives-cleanup
scenarios.action: delete the handle files only, save again

scenarios.name: context-mismatch
scenarios.after: argument error: rerun the original query

scenarios.name: account-mismatch
scenarios.start: handle 5 bound to context X for account 111
scenarios.action: load 5 with context X for account 222

scenarios.name: expired
scenarios.start: handle 5 created longer ago than the TTL
scenarios.after: argument error: expired, rerun the original query

scenarios.name: older-format
scenarios.start: handle 5 written with an older format
scenarios.after: argument error: from an earlier version

scenarios.name: not-a-number
scenarios.after: argument error before touching the filesystem

protection.fact: Account protection state is written atomically (temporary file, fsync, replace). State that cannot be read counts as blocked (fail closed). The next allowed time is recorded before a request starts, so a process killed mid-request cannot erase it. A checkpoint blocks until a person clears it; a rate limit blocks for 30 minutes. Requests are spaced 1-2 seconds apart at random. Check, budget, pacing, the request, its classification and a new block happen under one cross-process lock.

scenarios.name: pace-waits
scenarios.after: the request starts no earlier than that time

scenarios.name: pace-recorded-before-request
scenarios.action: request that is killed before it returns
scenarios.after: pace file holds a time 1-2 s after the request started

scenarios.name: block-recorded-inside-lock
scenarios.action: two processes; the first gets a checkpoint
scenarios.after: the second sees the block before making its request

scenarios.name: rate-limit-sets-30-minutes
scenarios.action: a response classified as rate limit
